'''Difficulty''' in [[Matcha Flavoured]] changes much more than in vanilla ''Minecraft''. Besides the vanilla effects, the world's difficulty decides how hostile [[mobs]] are modified when they spawn, how many hearts a [[death]] costs, whether the [[Wither effect]] takes hearts, and how far a player's maximum [[health]] can fall.

The pack describes its three difficulties in its language file as:<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref>
* '''Easy''': "For players who want to relax."
* '''Normal''': "For players who want a challenge."
* '''Hard''': "For players who want an unfair challenge."

== Mechanics ==
=== Reading the difficulty ===
The pack reads the world's difficulty only when the datapack loads, and prints it to chat: "Your gamemode is '''Easy'''", "'''Normal'''" or "'''Hard'''", followed by "(You can change this in the world settings, make sure you reload the world after)".<ref name="load">{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/load.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/scoreboard/create_scoreboards.mcfunction}}</ref> After changing the difficulty, the world has to be reloaded (with <code>/reload</code>, by rejoining, or by restarting the server) for the pack's own rules to follow. Until then, the pack keeps using the old difficulty while vanilla uses the new one.

=== Automatic increase ===
On Normal, the difficulty is raised to Hard automatically when any player's minimum hearts drops to 5, which happens at their fifth progression milestone. Every player sees "Game is now set to '''Hard'''". The change can be undone in the world settings.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/difficulty_scaling/increase_difficulty.mcfunction}}</ref> See [[Death#Minimum hearts]].

=== Mob modifications ===
{{Main|Spawning#Mob modifications}}
Each time one of the pack's "mundane hostile" mobs appears (zombie, husk, drowned, zombie villager, skeleton, stray, bogged, parched, creeper, spider, cave spider, slime, enderman, witch or silverfish), the pack checks it once and changes its attributes according to the difficulty.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/entity_type/mundane_hostiles.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/modify_mob.mcfunction}}</ref> Mobs not listed in the table keep their vanilla attributes. A dash means the vanilla value is kept.

Easy is close to vanilla mob behavior: zombies, husks and spiders are left unchanged, and only skeletons, creepers, cave spiders, silverfish and baby zombies are weakened. The Normal and Hard skeleton changes replace the skeleton's bow with a new one that has only Punch.

== History ==
{{History|
{{History line|1.10|Difficulty support added: the difficulty now changes mob behavior, health and damage. Easy is described as "essentially vanilla mob behaviour". Beating the Ender Dragon raises the difficulty.}}
{{History line|1.12|Husks slowed on Normal; husk attack damage lowered from 15 to 10 on Normal and from 20 to 15 on Hard.}}
{{History line|1.12.1-alpha|Killing the dragon no longer raises the difficulty on Normal; progression through advancements does instead. Baby zombies, husks and drowned have 2 hearts on Easy. Husk health on Normal lowered from 40 to 30.}}
{{History line|1.12.2|Hard husks slowed slightly. The Wither effect takes hearts, except on Easy. Easy guarantees at least 10 hearts.}}
}}

== Trivia ==
* The 1.10 release notes warn: "If you are playing on HARD, SET IT BACK TO NORMAL, unless you want to be angry".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=If you are playing on HARD, SET IT BACK TO NORMAL, unless you want to be angry}}</ref>
* The chat message calls the difficulty the "gamemode".
* An unused function would give Normal baby zombies {{Hp|5}}; Normal actually uses the shared Easy and Normal function, which gives {{Hp|4}}.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/normal_modifications/modify_baby_zombies.mcfunction}}</ref>
